Singapore Climate Trends (2020–2024)

Author

priya

Published

March 22, 2025

Modified

last-modified

1. Overview

This report explores weather patterns across various Singapore stations between 2020 and 2024. Using the cleaned dataset weather_data_clean.csv, we analyze rainfall and temperature variations across years, months, and stations.

2. Load Libraries and Data

Show code 
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)

weather <- read_csv("C:/privatejet/ISSS608/Take-Home_Ex/Take-home_Ex03/data/weather_data_clean.csv")

# Convert Date column to Date type
weather$Date <- ymd(weather$Date)

# Extract Year, Month, Day
weather <- weather %>%
  mutate(Year = year(Date),
         Month = month(Date, label = TRUE),
         Day = day(Date)) %>%
  filter(Year >= 2020 & Year <= 2024)

3. Annual Rainfall Trend (2020–2024)

Show code 
annual_rainfall <- weather %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(TotalRainfall = sum(`Daily Rainfall Total (mm)`, na.rm = TRUE))

ggplot(annual_rainfall, aes(x = Year, y = TotalRainfall)) +
  geom_col(fill = "skyblue") +
  labs(title = "Total Rainfall per Year (2020–2024)",
       x = "Year", y = "Total Rainfall (mm)") +
  theme_minimal()

4. Violin Plot of Mean Temperature by Station

Show code 
plot_data <- weather %>% filter(!is.na(`Mean Temperature (°C)`))

plot_ly(data = plot_data,
        x = ~Station,
        y = ~`Mean Temperature (°C)`,
        type = 'violin',
        box = list(visible = TRUE),
        meanline = list(visible = TRUE),
        marker = list(opacity = 0.5,
                      color = 'lightblue',
                      line = list(width = 0.5, color = 'darkblue')),
        color = ~Station) %>%
  layout(title = "Mean Temperature Distribution by Station",
         xaxis = list(title = "Station", tickangle = 45),
         yaxis = list(title = "Mean Temperature (°C)"))

5. Monthly Rainfall Pattern (Across Years)

Show code 
monthly_avg <- weather %>%
  group_by(Year, Month) %>%
  summarise(AvgRainfall = mean(`Daily Rainfall Total (mm)`, na.rm = TRUE))

ggplot(monthly_avg, aes(x = Month, y = AvgRainfall, group = Year, color = as.factor(Year))) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  labs(title = "Average Monthly Rainfall (2020–2024)",
       x = "Month", y = "Average Daily Rainfall (mm)", color = "Year") +
  theme_minimal()

6. Conclusion

From the visualizations, we observe yearly fluctuations in rainfall and distinct temperature distributions among stations. The violin plot reveals how certain stations experience broader temperature ranges. Monthly patterns suggest rainfall peaks during specific monsoon periods.

Further analysis could explore wind patterns or extreme weather events using this same dataset.
